reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Firework Finale on Nibbit, spending 3 Sparks for 18 damage and exhausting it. Then I played Bag of Tricks on Nibbit and chose Place 1 Bomb dealing 5. Then I played Quick Fuse on Nibbit to detonate that Bomb for 5 damage. Finally I played Duck and Cover for 5 Block.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered using Bag of Tricks' other option, Spend 3 Sparks: place 3 Bombs dealing 5, followed by Quick Fuse and Duck and Cover. That would use the same 3 Sparks to place 3 Bombs instead of playing Firework Finale, but the Firework Finale plus one Bomb line deals more damage on the information given.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the 3-Bomb option from Bag of Tricks, including the two extra Bombs that option would place, because Firework Finale consumes the same 3 Sparks. It also gave up keeping Firework Finale available by exhausting it.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. The only intent-sensitive card in the hand is Duck and Cover, and it has no meaningful downside here: it costs 1 Energy that would otherwise go unused, and the rest of the line is unchanged. A different telegraphed intent would not make me drop the damage sequence or the Block.
